verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four plants are measured before they were fed: the tomato was 'fed 3 August' but scored 'by 20 June', and the oak was 'fed 2 May' but scored 'by 19 April'. The other two cases (8 January to 26 February, 7 October to 24 November) run forward, so the outcome in half the cases precedes the intervention.

'The central syllabus doubled coursework's share of the final grade against the previous year, and every section was marked to that central syllabus' names an alternative cause that reaches all four sections in exactly the year-on-year window being compared; doubling coursework's weight is enough on its own to raise completion, so the lab kit is not isolated.

'Timings cover the runs that reported a finish time, and about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none' means the averages are computed on only five-sixths of the runs, excluding precisely the runs most likely to have gone wrong or run long; an 8- or 9-minute drop could come entirely from which runs fell out of the denominator.

'Absence figures cover the pupils enrolled for the whole term, and about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through' means a fifth of each cohort is dropped from the figures, and part-way leavers are the pupils with the worst attendance; excluding them alone lowers measured absence by more than the 4-7 percent reported.
